newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hagemeyer's HCL to seek Hong Kong listing.
newsitem.headline: Hagemeyer's HCL to seek Hong Kong listing.

text.p: Trading company Hagemeyer NV said on Thursday it would probably seek a bourse listing for its subsidiary HCL in Hong Kong when it finds a large acquisition in Asia.

Hagemeyer recently bought the remaining 50 percent in its Hong Kong-based joint venture Hagemeyer Cosa Liebermann (HCL) from Swiss Anova and told a news conference in February that it would seek a bourse listing for HCL within a few years.
"We would like to link a listing to a happening in the field of an acquisition in Asia by which HCL would expand substantially," Hagemeyer chairman Andrew Land told Reuters.
"If the acquisition is substantial we will also issue new shares," Land said.
HCL's trading business, which includes sports equipment, lifestyle products, household appliances and photographic equipment, currently has an annual turnover of 1.5 to 1.6 billion guilders.
"Turnover should expand to 3.0 billion guilders or more within a few years," Land said.
Land said it was aiming for a listing in Hong Kong to give the company a more local face.
"We want to integrate HCL more in the local Asian market," he said, in order to emphasise its presence in the market and to make it easier for Hagemeyer to attract high quality personnel.
Hong Kong's First Pacific Co owns an economic stake of approximately 36 percent in Hagemeyer.
